text:
dave_customer: Hey, we started seeing a bunch of 401s right after using the dashboard "Clone key" button to make an env-specific key. Calls that used to work now return \"invalid_api_key\". No code changes on our side.

alice_support: Ugh, sorry about that. Can you paste the exact curl you used and any request-id from the response headers? Also which deployment (hosted vs dedicated)?

dave_customer: Hosted. Example:
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: ApiKey sk_clone_7Xy9\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-request-id: req_9x3a2
content-type: application/json
{\"error\":{\"code\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"Invalid API key\"}}
```

alice_support: Thanks. Escalating to eng and attaching the request-id. @charlie_engineer can you triage?

charlie_engineer: I pulled the auth logs for req_9x3a2. Interesting: there are two rows in the api_keys table with the same key_id value (sk_clone_7Xy9) but different secret_hashes and different internal ids. The verifier lookup was returning the older row which no longer matches the secret the customer used.

charlie_engineer: Quick repro I ran: create key via dashboard -> use clone action -> DB shows duplicate key_id. Query:
```
SELECT internal_id, key_id, secret_hash, created_at FROM api_keys WHERE key_id='sk_clone_7Xy9';
-- results:
-- internal_id=1023, key_id=sk_clone_7Xy9, secret_hash=HASH_A, created_at=2024-04-02T09:11:02Z
-- internal_id=2048, key_id=sk_clone_7Xy9, secret_hash=HASH_B, created_at=2024-04-02T09:11:04Z
```

charlie_engineer: Root cause: dashboard clone flow attempted to insert new row but a race in the client-side id generation allowed reuse of the key_id from the source; no DB unique constraint existed on key_id in that release. Auth layer selects by key_id and compares hashes; picking the wrong row leads to mismatch and 401.

ben_infra: We have a quick mitigation: add a read-path disambiguation to prefer the most recent created_at for duplicated key_id until we enforce uniqueness. Also rolling out a migration to dedupe duplicates and add a unique constraint. Patch queued: auth -> prefer latest when duplicates found + alert.

charlie_engineer: For affected customers: advise immediate rotate/recreate keys from the dashboard, then delete the old duplicate entries via admin console. I'm adding a safe dedupe job that maps duplicates to single canonical key (most recent) and rotates the older ones.

alice_support: @dave_customer, can you rotate the cloned key to a fresh key for now? Steps: open dashboard -> API keys -> Revoke sk_clone_7Xy9 -> Create new key -> update your env var. If you want us to rotate for you we can, just confirm. :thumbsup:

dave_customer: Will do that now. Appreciate the speedy triage. Can you also confirm whether any calls were authenticated with the old (stolen) secret? We didn't share it externally.

charlie_engineer: No evidence of misuse in access logs for that key_id window. The error pattern indicates mismatched secret, not accepted usage. Still rotating is safest. We'll deploy the unique-constraint migration within 24 hours and run the dedupe job overnight.

deploy-bot: deploy auth-prefer-latest-dedupe-job v1.2.1 started to canary (region us-west-2) at 2024-04-02T12:34:00Z

dave_customer: Rotation completed, calls back to normal. Thank you all.

alice_support: Great — marking this resolved for now. We'll keep you posted once the migration/dedupe lands globally. :white_check_mark:
